title: GC Enterprise Architecture self-assessment
provenance: Imported by tools/import-rubric.mjs from Dan's GC_EA_Assessment_Tool workbook (6 sheets) in "EARB target state knowledge base". Questions, section names, section weights, domain weights and the 0-10 ladder are all his. Added by us and marked as such: lifecycle stages, the stage rule on "Defining the Current State" sections, and the routing bands.
dlgBaseUrlNote: The guide, on GitHub Pages for now. Each stage points at its own page there.
importWarnings: Business Architecture: the section weights in the workbook add up to 80%, not 100%. The missing 20 points are shared out across the 6 sections that are there, in proportion, so the domain still scores out of 10. Worth checking whether a section was left out of the export.

anchors.name: Absent
anchors.label: No formal architecture. Capabilities are missing, and manual workarounds are the only way to achieve business outcomes.

anchors.name: Critical Gaps
anchors.label: A skeleton exists, but core capabilities (like security or data integrity) are missing. High risk of systemic failure.

anchors.name: Fragmented
anchors.label: Capabilities exist in "silos." They are inconsistent, undocumented, and require constant manual intervention to stay synchronized.

anchors.name: Emergent
anchors.label: Core capabilities are present but brittle. The architecture meets the "happy path" but fails under stress or edge cases.

anchors.name: Defined
anchors.label: The architecture meets basic functional requirements. Documentation exists, but Quality Attributes (scalability, maintainability) are an afterthought.

anchors.name: Integrated
anchors.label: This is the Baseline. All desired capabilities are present and connected. The system is stable and performs as expected under normal conditions.

anchors.name: Managed
anchors.label: Capabilities are monitored and measured. The architecture can handle predictable growth and has basic fault tolerance.

anchors.name: Scalable & Secure
anchors.label: The architecture is "hardened." It handles bursts in demand effortlessly and has proactive security measures built into the design.

anchors.name: Agile/Extensible
anchors.label: The architecture is modular. Adding a new desired capability does not require a rewrite; the system is designed to be plugged into and extended.

anchors.name: Predictive
anchors.label: The architecture uses telemetry and AI/ML to anticipate needs (e.g., auto-scaling before a spike or self-healing before a crash).

anchors.name: Symbiotic
anchors.label: The "North Star" state. The architecture and business strategy are one. The system is so flexible it can pivot to entirely new business models with minimal architectural friction.

maturityBands.label: Leading Practice
maturityBands.detail: Predictive, self-optimizing, fully aligned with business strategy.

maturityBands.label: Advanced
maturityBands.detail: Hardened, scalable, and modular. Demonstrably high-quality architecture.

maturityBands.label: Baseline Ready
maturityBands.detail: Core capabilities present and stable. Meets minimum GC EA expectations.

maturityBands.label: Developing
maturityBands.detail: Foundational elements exist but architecture is immature and at risk under stress.

maturityBands.label: Critical Risk
maturityBands.detail: Immediate intervention required. Core capabilities absent or severely compromised.

maturityBandsNote: Dan's own reference guide, from the Summary Dashboard sheet.

bands.label: Showcase
bands.routing: No board slot needed. TBS may ask to showcase this work.

bands.label: Hall pass
bands.routing: Suggested: no GC EARB appearance required. Subject to audit sample.

bands.label: Routine
bands.routing: Suggested: no board time. Assessor spot-check only.

bands.label: Bring it to the board
bands.routing: Suggested: attend GC EARB. Come and tell us why, and what the plan is.

bandsNote: ROUTING, not maturity, and provisional. Dan named three numbers out loud on 2026-08-26: above roughly 60% is an automatic hall pass, around 8.5 is worth showcasing, and around 2 out of 10 means come and explain. He also said the 4, 5, 6 middle is not worth board time. The 3.0 line between "come and explain" and "no board time" is OURS, interpolated to bridge the 2 he named and the 4 he named. He has not seen it. None of these are signed off. The maturity labels above are his.
stageMultipliersNote: Our addition. Lifecycle stage is not captured in the current process at all - Dan named it as the key missing field. Only "Defining the Current State" sections carry a rule so far.

lifecycleStages.label: Discovery
lifecycleStages.blurb: Understanding the problem. There may be no current solution to describe yet.

lifecycleStages.label: Alpha
lifecycleStages.blurb: Testing whether an approach can work, with real users.

lifecycleStages.label: Beta
lifecycleStages.blurb: Building the real thing in public, at growing scale.

lifecycleStages.label: Stabilization
lifecycleStages.blurb: In service, settling down. Costs and operations should be known.

lifecycleStages.label: Maturity
lifecycleStages.blurb: In service, steady state. Everything should be documented and measured.

lifecycleStages.label: Sunset
lifecycleStages.blurb: Replacing or retiring. Dependencies and data disposition matter most.

phases.name: Create
phases.blurb: Being built, and not in service yet.

domains.label: Business Architecture
domains.description: Connecting strategy to execution through structured design

questions.text: How thoroughly has the current state of this solution been documented, including all processes, data flows, and system dependencies?
What entities (data objects, records, clients, files) are currently produced, managed, or maintained by this solution?
Have all roles and responsibilities across stakeholders, operators, and service consumers been identified, documented, and formally accepted?
How well understood is the criticality of this solution to Government of Canada program delivery and citizen outcomes?
Are all sub-components of the current solution assessed for their individual criticality, availability, and risk exposure?
What is the current level of utilization and demand for the solution (transaction volumes, active users, peak load)?
What is the known availability, uptime, and service continuity record of the current solution?
How well understood are the total lifecycle costs — including build, operate, maintain, and decommission — of the current solution?
What are the current unit economics (cost per transaction, cost per entity managed) and how are they tracked?
How mature and current are the performance indicators for this solution, and what trends do they reflect?
Is the lifespan and full lifecycle of the solution mapped out, and is the current position within that lifecycle known?
What major events (technology refresh, contract renewal, legislative changes) are on the horizon for this solution?
How well understood are the specific skills, staffing levels, and capacity requirements to operate and evolve this solution?
How are universal requirements — accessibility, official languages, inclusion, and privacy — currently addressed in the solution?
How clearly and completely has the core business problem been defined and agreed upon by all stakeholders?
Is there a documented business case that articulates the expected value, outcomes, and measurable benefits of the proposed solution?
How well do the proposed solution capabilities map to the GC Business Capability Model and existing enterprise services?
Have value streams been fully mapped, showing how business capabilities deliver outcomes to clients and citizens?
Is the solution design driven by defined user personas, journeys, and evidence-based user research?
How clearly are the target service levels, response times, and quality benchmarks defined for the proposed solution?
Has the solution's criticality to GC program delivery been assessed, and does the architecture reflect that criticality?
Is there a funding model and sourcing strategy that is sustainable across the full lifecycle of the solution?
How well is the talent strategy defined, including required skills, existing capacity, training pipeline, and long-term retention?
Is a demand forecast available, and does the solution design account for projected growth and usage variability?
How well is the solution integrated within the broader GC enterprise ecosystem and aligned with whole-of-government priorities?
Is the solution designed to maximize reuse of existing GC shared services and platforms before building new capabilities?
How transparent is the solution design — is it documented, accessible, and understandable to those who rely on it?
Have user personas, stories, and journeys been mapped and validated through direct engagement with actual users and stakeholders?
Are there formal, repeatable mechanisms to capture client, user, and stakeholder needs on a continuous basis?
How mature are feedback loops between the delivery team and end users, including Communities of Practice and regular reviews?
Are all roles, accountabilities, and decision rights across the solution ecosystem clearly documented in a RACI or equivalent model?
Is solution documentation, interactive guidance, and self-service assistance available and actively maintained for all user types?
How transparent is the operational status of the solution, including an offering roadmap and historical event schedule?
Are performance metrics (NPS, CSAT, CES, usage rates, drop-off rates) defined, measured, and reported back to stakeholders?
Does the solution support multi-channel delivery patterns (web, chat, phone, in-person) that reflect real user demand?
How mature are personalization, predictive analytics, or AI-assisted capabilities within the solution offering?
Are Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and Service Level Agreements (SLAs) formally defined, monitored, and reported?
Is there end-to-end instrumentation of delivery processes, enabling real-time performance monitoring and visualization?
How well are costs, prices, and unit economics tracked and published, enabling informed investment decisions?
Are client satisfaction scores (CSAT, NPS, or equivalent) captured systematically and acted upon?
How are quality and error rates measured, tracked, and used to drive continuous improvement?
Are response times, total transaction times, and execution time variance measured and within defined thresholds?
Is trend analysis performed regularly on key metrics to anticipate performance changes and drive proactive action?
Are periodic evaluations of continuing business need performed to assess whether the solution still justifies its cost?
How well-defined is the delivery pipeline, including deployment cadence, automation, rollback procedures, and success rates?
Are skills requirements, staffing levels, and a training and improvement pipeline in place to sustain operations?
Is there an established and confirmed funding strategy, including lifecycle funding beyond the initial build phase?
How mature and tested is the incident management, business continuity, and disaster recovery planning for this solution?
Is the infrastructure and technology acquisition strategy defined, including procurement pathways and lead times?
Has a formal threat and risk assessment (including sovereignty and security classification) been completed and reviewed?
How deep and well-prioritized is the feature and requirements backlog, and does it reflect validated stakeholder needs?
Are there operational runbooks, monitoring dashboards, and on-call processes in place to support production operations?
Is there a clearly defined governance model with accountable decision-makers for the solution's direction and performance?
How well does the solution align with the GC Digital Operations Strategic Plan and departmental enterprise strategy?
Is there a published roadmap with near, medium, and long-term milestones that is communicated to stakeholders?
How mature is the change management process, including impact assessment, approval workflows, and communication plans?
Are compliance requirements (legal, regulatory, policy, accessibility, bilingualism) formally tracked and verified?
Is there a formal risk register maintained for the solution, with assigned owners and documented mitigation strategies?
How well is vendor and third-party relationship governance defined, including performance monitoring and exit strategies?
Is there a documented and approved data governance model aligned with the solution's information and privacy requirements?
How well does the solution contribute to GC-wide shared service consolidation and enterprise architecture objectives?

domains.label: Data & Information Architecture
domains.description: Turning raw data into trusted, connected insights

questions.text: How well documented are current data models, entity relationships, and data-sharing agreements?
What is the degree of data fragmentation, duplication, and inconsistency across the current solution and its dependencies?
How well understood are data volumes, growth rates, residency requirements, and encryption posture?
Is the lifespan and full data lifecycle — from creation to disposition — mapped and governed?
Are data formats proprietary or based on open, interoperable standards?
How open and transparent is data publication, and is a default-open approach applied where appropriate?
Are analytics and trend analysis capabilities available to support decision-making from current data assets?
How mature are data access controls, auditing mechanisms, and the ability to trace who accessed what and when?
How interoperable is the current data environment with other GC systems, programs, and platforms?
Is there a formal, documented data model that reflects all key entities, relationships, attributes, and business rules?
How mature is master data management — are authoritative data sources identified, maintained, and trusted?
Is data lifecycle governance established, covering creation, versioning, archiving, and secure disposition?
Are international and GC data standards applied (e.g., ISO, DCAT, NIEM, GC Open Data Directive)?
How well defined is data lineage — can the origin, transformation, and movement of data be traced end-to-end?
Is comprehensive metadata management in place, enabling data discovery, classification, and contextual understanding?
How mature is data quality management — are completeness, accuracy, consistency, and timeliness measured and enforced?
Is data instrumentation in place to capture operational telemetry, audit records, and system-generated metadata?
Are data read/write performance requirements (volumes, IOPS, movement patterns) understood and architecturally addressed?
Is there a strategy for structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data that applies consistent governance across all types?
How well is data residency managed — are intentional copies of data tracked, controlled, and compliant with policy?
Does the architecture support event-driven data integration patterns and real-time data processing where needed?
Has a Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) been completed, and does the architecture reflect its recommendations?
Is Privacy by Design embedded throughout the solution, from data collection through to disposition?
How mature is data categorization — are all data assets classified by sensitivity, and is handling appropriate to classification?
Is encryption applied at rest, in transit, and in processing for all data at the appropriate sensitivity level?
Are data sovereignty requirements met — is there full awareness of where data resides, crosses borders, and is subject to foreign law?
Are data retention and disposition policies enforced, including secure deletion and legal hold capabilities?
How well are collection limitation principles applied — is only necessary data collected, with informed consent where required?
Is there a documented breach response plan, and has it been tested?
Are access controls enforced at the data level, ensuring role-based and attribute-based access is actively governed?
Does the data architecture align with FAIR principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable)?
Are APIs and data-sharing interfaces standards-based and documented, enabling downstream consumption without tight coupling?
How accessible is data to authorized consumers, including other departments, partners, and (where appropriate) the public?
Is there a designated data owner and data steward for each key dataset, with documented accountability?
How mature is the data governance framework — does it cover policies, standards, roles, dispute resolution, and enforcement?
Are data governance decisions transparent and auditable, including any changes to data models, access rules, or classifications?
Is there a process to ensure data governance keeps pace with legislative changes (Privacy Act, Access to Information, Bill C-27)?
How well is data quality monitored, reported on, and escalated when thresholds are breached?
Is there a regular data audit process to validate compliance with policies, identify orphaned data, and assess data health?
Is the current application solution fully documented, including architecture diagrams, data flows, and integration points?
How well is the current system instrumented — are resource allocation, consumption, and application health monitored?
What is the outstanding technical debt, and is it formally tracked in a backlog with prioritization?
When are major software contracts expiring, and is there a renewal or replacement strategy in place?
What known security vulnerabilities exist in the current solution, and what is the remediation status?
How well understood are the delivery pipeline properties — maturity, automation, deployment frequency, and failure rate?
What is the degree of vendor or technology lock-in, and are exit/migration pathways understood?
Are all upstream and downstream application dependencies mapped and current?
What is the known backlog of defects, flaws, and unresolved issues, and how is it managed?
Is the application type (COTS, configured, custom-built, low/no-code, assembled) clearly defined and justified?
Is the delivery methodology (agile, waterfall, hybrid) appropriate to the solution's context and documented?
How software-defined is the solution — are configuration, policy, and infrastructure managed as code?
Is the application designed with capabilities-based modularity, enabling components to be replaced independently?
How are interoperability interfaces between internal components and external applications exposed and governed?
Is intellectual property ownership clear, and are code licensing obligations tracked and managed?
How mature is code reuse — is there a shared code repository, automated integration, and published component catalogue?
What is the lowest required integration level (container, VM/OS, physical hardware), and is it minimized where possible?
Are volume, redundancy, elasticity, scalability, throttling, and observability requirements defined and implemented?
Is the application designed as external-facing, internal enterprise, or administrative — and is the design tailored accordingly?
How mature is the DevSecOps pipeline — including continuous integration, continuous deployment, automated testing, and security gates?
Is test coverage defined, measured, and enforced — including unit, integration, regression, performance, and security testing?
How well are coding standards, frameworks, and languages documented, enforced, and aligned with GC guidance?
Are accessibility standards (WCAG 2.1 AA or equivalent) embedded in the development and QA process?
Is there an algorithmic impact assessment (AIA) process in place for any AI/ML components in the application?
How mature is the code review and peer review process, and is it consistently applied?
Are application performance benchmarks established, tested against in CI/CD, and used to gate deployments?
Is observability (logging, tracing, metrics) built into the application architecture from the start?
Has a multi-disciplinary team — including business, security, privacy, data, and technology — been engaged in solution design?
Were enterprise contracts and procurement pathways (GC-wide standing offers, task authorizations) explored before custom sourcing?
Was optionality fully investigated — including multi-vendor, open source, and homegrown options — with a documented rationale?
Is a Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) model available that includes build, operate, maintain, licensing, and exit costs?
How well are digital sovereignty considerations addressed — are GC data and systems protected from foreign jurisdiction risk?
Is the solution designed to integrate with GC-wide shared services (Sign-In Canada, GC Notify, GC Forms, etc.) where applicable?
How well does the solution avoid unnecessary duplication with existing GC capabilities and investments?
Is there a clear strategy for AI integration — including use of GC Foundation Models and GC AI Compute infrastructure?
Is the solution designed to be decommissioned or migrated, with a documented sunset and transition strategy?
How well are supply chain security risks addressed in the sourcing and integration of third-party components?
Are all details of the current solution's hosting environment — hardware, software, network, and configuration — fully documented?
Is the current solution healthy, with no critical alerts, capacity issues, or unresolved infrastructure-level incidents?
Are there any imminent changes to consumed infrastructure services, and is the solution prepared for those transitions?
Is the lifespan of the solution shorter than that of the infrastructure — and if not, is an upgrade plan in the backlog?
How well-informed is the team about their infrastructure service provider's roadmap, changes, and service performance?
Can infrastructure be ordered and provisioned on demand, and what lead time is required?
Is there a clear inventory of all infrastructure components, including versions, patch levels, and support status?
Is the physical hosting model (on-premise EDC, public cloud, private cloud, hybrid) clearly justified and documented?
Is the decision between shared and dedicated hardware documented with supporting rationale for cost, isolation, and performance?
Are physical kiosks, IoT devices, or specialized hardware requirements identified and architecturally accommodated?
How well does the design leverage GC-wide service consolidation, shared footprint, and enterprise infrastructure services?
Are elasticity, burst capacity, and auto-scaling requirements defined and architecturally implemented?
Are High-Performance Computing (HPC) and edge computing needs assessed and addressed where applicable?
Is GC AI Compute (dedicated GC-owned/controlled GPU infrastructure) considered and evaluated as a first option for AI workloads?
Are bandwidth, latency, and network connectivity requirements defined and met by the infrastructure design?
Are storage volumes, IOPS, throughput, and data tiering requirements specified and provisioned appropriately?
Is the deployment model designed to meet availability, recovery time, and recovery point objectives?
Is configuration and infrastructure managed as code (IaC/CaC), enabling reproducible and auditable deployments?
How well does the team understand and apply GC-relevant infrastructure design patterns and reference architectures?
Does the architecture embrace composable, modular designs and event-driven models where appropriate?
Is interoperability and containerization baked into the infrastructure design from the beginning?
Is there a documented plan and roadmap for quantum and post-quantum cryptography readiness?
How mature is the use of platform engineering practices — are developer-facing platforms self-service and well-governed?
Are orchestration and container management (e.g., Kubernetes) used appropriately and configured to GC standards?
Are resilience requirements (availability tiers, fault tolerance, geo-redundancy) formally defined and validated in design?
Is the solution's data sovereignty posture clearly documented, including data residency and foreign access risk mitigation?
How mature is the zero-trust security architecture — is authentication, authorization, and segmentation enforced throughout?
Is encryption applied appropriately at rest, in transit, and in processing, using GC-approved cryptographic standards?
Has a Threat and Risk Assessment (TRA) or Security Assessment and Authorization (SA&A) been completed and reflected in design?
Are security controls validated through automated security testing, vulnerability scanning, and penetration testing?
Is there a documented and tested disaster recovery plan, with defined RTO and RPO that align to business requirements?
Are GC Cloud Guardrails and security baseline configurations implemented and continuously validated?
Are real-time monitoring, alerting, and incident response capabilities in place and actively used?
Is activity auditing implemented at the infrastructure level, enabling forensic investigation and compliance verification?
How mature is the FinOps practice — are cloud and infrastructure costs tracked, attributed, optimized, and reported?
Is there infrastructure-level observability (metrics, logs, traces) that provides end-to-end system visibility?
Are resource governance policies enforced — including tagging, cost allocation, and access to shared infrastructure?
Is there a continuous business need (CBN) process to evaluate whether infrastructure investment remains justified?
How mature is the infrastructure change management process — are changes reviewed, approved, and traceable?
